candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
verified_facts: Official Environment Agency composite DTM covers about 99% of England at 1m spatial resolution.
Surface objects are removed to create a bare-earth terrain model.
The composite uses time-stamped and National LIDAR Programme surveys; repeat coverage uses the newest best-resolution data and resampling uses bilinear interpolation.
The metadata index is required to identify the survey used at a location.
semantic_limits: Composite 1m resolution does not by itself identify the contributing survey for a parcel.
Bilinear-resampled composite cells remain derived observations and their survey lineage must stay explicit.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 2m
verified_facts: Official Environment Agency DTM product covers about 99% of England at 2m spatial resolution.
The DTM excludes surface objects and is derived from time-stamped and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where data was resampled the product uses bilinear interpolation.
The dataset states a vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15cm RMSE and exposes WMS/WCS/WMTS plus metadata-index services.
semantic_limits: The 2m product is a secondary comparison for this slot and must not replace the 1m primary source.
The stated RMSE is a dataset/survey quality specification, not a parcel-specific confidence interval.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles
verified_facts: The time-stamped DTM archive contains site-specific Environment Agency raster surveys at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m depending on project requirements.
DTM tiles remove surface objects and are distributed as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files aligned to the OS Grid.
Elevations are in metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and the transformation is survey-period specific.
Metadata index catalogues provide survey dates, resolution and transformation/geoid information for each location.
semantic_limits: Time-stamped availability does not prove which survey contributed to a composite cell without an exact metadata feature match.
Survey-specific transform/geoid metadata must not be inferred from the composite filename alone.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR DSM Time Stamped Tiles
verified_facts: The time-stamped DSM archive contains site-specific raster surveys at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m.
DSM includes vehicles, buildings, vegetation and terrain surface rather than bare earth only.
Data are GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files aligned to the OS Grid and referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
Coverage metadata is available in several vector formats and through map/feature services.
semantic_limits: DSM values must be excluded from the primary bare-earth height-difference calculation.
DSM metadata can support lineage checks but cannot be substituted for DTM samples.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud
verified_facts: The official point-cloud archive contains large sets of x,y,z points and attributes from Environment Agency surveys.
Time-stamped DSM and DTM raster products are derived from point-cloud data.
Point-cloud availability extends back to 2006 but historic archiving means a matching point cloud may not exist for every surface-model survey.
Coverage metadata can be downloaded as GeoJSON, GeoPackage, shapefile or geodatabase.
semantic_limits: Point-cloud absence must not be treated as proof that a raster survey is invalid.
Point-cloud evidence is lineage/support evidence unless the exact contributing survey is matched.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite First Return Digital Surface Model (FZ_DSM) - 1m
verified_facts: The 1m first-return DSM covers about 99% of England and includes objects where the first or only return hits them.
It is built from National LIDAR Programme surveys captured from November 2016 to May 2022.
Survey overlaps are merged using feathering to reduce small elevation differences.
Metadata index catalogues identify the survey used at a location.
semantic_limits: First-return DSM is not a bare-earth DTM and is excluded from primary terrain extrema.
Feathering is a merge operation and must not be interpreted as raw survey precision.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: National LIDAR Programme
verified_facts: The National LIDAR Programme provides 1m elevation data for all of England.
Phase 1 divided England into 302 survey blocks captured in winter campaigns between 2017 and February 2023.
Repeat blocks receive incrementing phase numbers rather than implying a fixed rolling recapture programme.
Products are published in 5km OS-grid tiles and filenames include survey id, grid reference and survey dates; an index catalogue provides survey-specific tile information.
semantic_limits: Programme/block existence is not parcel-specific contributing-survey proof.
The exact survey id and phase must come from matched metadata rather than nearest-block inference.

candidates.name: HM Land Registry plans: boundaries (practice guide 40, supplement 3)
verified_facts: The guidance was updated 1 June 2026.
Most registered titles show general boundaries under section 60(1) of the Land Registration Act 2002.
HM Land Registry states there is no standard tolerance, measurement or ratio between a general boundary on a title plan and the legal boundary.
A legal boundary is an exact line and is rarely identified with precision on the ground or in conveyances.
semantic_limits: A general title-plan or index-polygon edge cannot be treated as a survey-grade exact parcel boundary.
Boundary uncertainty is horizontal/legal geometry uncertainty and must not be converted into vertical terrain error.

candidates.name: HM Land Registry plans: title plan (practice guide 40, supplement 5)
verified_facts: A title plan supports the property description in the register and identifies the general extent of land in a registered title.
All title plans show general boundaries unless a boundary has been determined under section 60.
Dimensions copied from older deed plans can be unreliable because the physical reference points may have changed or disappeared.
semantic_limits: Title-plan dimensions must not be promoted to exact polygon geometry without supporting determined-boundary evidence.
The title plan must be interpreted together with the register and relevant filed documents.

candidates.name: Apply to record the exact boundary
verified_facts: A registered proprietor can apply to record the exact boundary as a determined boundary.
The application requires evidence and a plan showing the determined boundary, with GOV.UK recommending a chartered land surveyor prepare the plan.
The title plan and register can be checked to see whether a determined boundary is already recorded.
semantic_limits: Absent determined-boundary evidence, ordinary title-plan or INSPIRE geometry remains non-exact for the legal line.
Determined-boundary status affects legal geometry confidence, not LiDAR vertical measurement accuracy.

revalidated_existing_sources.topic: EA vertical-accuracy limits remain survey-QC semantics
EA metadata-index feature matching remains mandatory
EA BNG/ODN/geoid lineage remains separate from terrain values
HMLR reprojection shift remains horizontal mapping uncertainty
EA Ground Truth remains survey-QC reference evidence
HMLR INSPIRE remains indicative extent and identifier aid
Determined-boundary evidence remains the exact-boundary gate
